regulatory_notes: The current standalone Chapter 2.11 PDF on the FSSAI compendium page does not print an explicit version/date label; PMSV therefore does not invent a version number and records the chapter as the current consolidated source verified on 2026-10-02.

FSSAI's current testing-fee document identifies the Chapter 2.11 products/standards as Baking Powder, Catechu, Gelatin, Silver Leaf, Pan Masala, Carob Powder, Dietary Fibre and Special dietary food with low sodium content.

FoSCoS guidance states Special dietary food with low sodium content is not itself listed as a standalone FoSCoS product; the corresponding food category is selected and the 2.11.9 process/composition standard applies additionally.

Historical labelling references inside Chapter 2.11 refer to the former Packaging and Labelling Regulations, 2011. PMSV does not use those historical references as the current labelling layer; current Labelling and Display Regulations must be evaluated separately.

common_rules.text: Applicable products shall comply with the current Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations.
Food additives are permitted only where allowed by the applicable product standard and Appendix A.

Current Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 apply; historical Chapter 2.11 references to the former Packaging and Labelling Regulations are retained only as source history.

horizontal_rules.name: Special Dietary Food with Low Sodium Content
horizontal_rules.foscos_mapping: No standalone FoSCoS product row. Apply to the corresponding underlying food category in addition to that food's own standard.

requirements.parameter: Sodium relative to comparable normal product as consumed
Sodium in final product as normally consumed
Sodium relative to comparable normal product as consumed
Sodium in final product as normally consumed

horizontal_rules.salt_substitute_rule: Salt substitutes conforming to 2.9.30(6) may be added at GMP.
chapter_label_requirements: Use the description 'low sodium' or 'very low sodium' according to the applicable class.
Declare sodium per 100 g and per specified serving.
Declare average carbohydrate, protein and fat per 100 g and energy value.
If a potassium salt substitute is used, declare total potassium as mg cation/100 g.
Declare sodium-chloride equivalent per serving and total NaCl in the pack.
Declare special storage conditions, where applicable.
horizontal_rules.labelling_validation_note: The chapter text contains historical references to the former 2011 labelling regulations. Numerical sodium criteria are structured; label enforcement must be reconciled against current Labelling and Display Regulations before hard-fail use.

standards.name: Baking Powder
standards.definition: A combination capable under baking conditions of yielding carbon dioxide, consisting of sodium bicarbonate, acid-reacting material, starch or other neutral material.
optional_neutral_materials: Edible starches from cereals, roots and tubers
Acid pectin and similar neutral materials
permitted_acidulants: Potassium bitartrate / potassium hydrogen tartrate (cream of tartar)

quality_rules.value: White free-flowing powder, free from off odour

standards.name: Catechu (Edible)
standards.definition: Dried aqueous extract prepared from the heartwood of Acacia catechu.

composition.parameter: Ash insoluble in HCl — dry basis
Ash insoluble in dilute HCl — Bhatti Katha — dry basis

standards.identity_test: 1% aqueous solution plus 0.1% ferric ammonium sulphate gives dark green colour, changing to purple on addition of sodium hydroxide.

standards.name: Gelatin
standards.definition: Purified product obtained by partial hydrolysis of collagen derived from animal skin, white connective tissues and bones.
quality_rules: Colourless or pale yellowish and translucent; sheets, flakes, shreds or coarse-to-fine powder; only slight characteristic odour/taste.
standards.distinction_note: This is animal-derived gelatin under 2.11.3. Gelatin from fish-processing waste is separately standardised under Chapter 2.6.1(25).

standards.name: Silver Leaf (Chandi-ka-warq)

quality_rules.value: Sheet of uniform thickness, free from creases and folds

prohibited_or_absent: Material of animal origin at any stage of manufacture
standards.contaminants: Current FSSAI Contaminants, Toxins and Residues requirements apply.

standards.name: Pan Masala
prohibited_or_absent: Tobacco as an ingredient of the FSSAI-standardised Pan Masala product

composition.parameter: Ash insoluble in dilute HCl — dry basis

standards.note: Separate state-level restrictions/prohibitions and other laws may apply to manufacture, storage, distribution or sale; this product-standard profile alone does not determine marketability in a specific state.

standards.name: Carob Powder
standards.definition: Powder obtained from roasted husk-free pods of Ceratonia siliqua.

standards.name: Dietary Fibre (Dextrin-soluble fibre)
standards.definition: Glucose polymer of natural origin obtained by dextrinification of acidified starch under specific dry-roasting conditions and further purification.

identity_parameters.value: Contains indigestible alpha- and beta-linkages in addition to digestible alpha-(1,4) and alpha-(1,6) linkages

permitted_foods: Flakes and ready-to-eat dry breakfast cereals
Table-top fibre as filler or carrier and cereals
Bakery products including biscuits, cookies, bread, cake mixes and pastries
Other products where dextrin is permitted under FSSAI regulations
standards.source_rule: Ingredient source (wheat/maize) shall be non-genetically modified according to the Chapter 2.11 text.

chapter_claim_text.threshold_text: Not less than 3 g/100 g or 1.5 g/100 kcal
Chapter text states not less than 3 g/100 g or 1.5 g/100 kcal and not more than 6 g/100 g or 3 g/100 kcal

standards.labelling_validation_note: Claim wording/thresholds originate from historical Chapter 2.11 text referencing the former 2011 labelling regulation. PMSV will not use them as current hard-fail claim rules until reconciled against the current Labelling and Display Regulations.
